the development of new scientific tools is the key factor in scientific revolutions in neuroscience, and that this development can be usefully described in terms of a problem, and two types of experimental hook.

the Kuhnian model of scientific revolutions does not apply to the actual revolutions in neuroscience, and that the development of a new experimental tool is the only way a new paradigm in neuroscience could ever be developed.

the development of new tools, and not with the development of competing paradigms.

the Kuhnian model does not apply to neuroscience revolutions.

the new tools are the key to neuroscience revolutions.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the development and application of new experimental tools is the driving force behind revolutions in neuroscience, and that Kuhn’s famous account is not the right model of scientific revolutions in neuroscience.

, in order to understand the nature and dynamics of revolutions in science, it is crucial to focus on the development of experimental tools, and to understand how they are designed to solve specific motivating problems.
